rows.scope: Annex I point 3.6.13 'Infant formulae, follow-on formulae, food for special medical purposes intended for infants and young children (3) and young-child formulae (4)', sub-point 3.6.13.3 'placed on the market as liquid'
rows.basis: The maximum level applies to the product as placed on the market (remark attached to 3.6.13). Value stated as 0,10 mg/kg.
rows.evidence: "3.6.13.3 placed on the market as liquid 0,10" (Annex I pt 3.6.13.3; consolidated 02023R0915 08.10.2025 p. 59; OJ L 2024/1987 p. 6/7)
rows.primary_source_used: raw/regulatory/eu/eu-2023-915-consolidated-2025-10-08.pdf (EUR-Lex consolidated text 02023R0915-20251008, consolidation date 08.10.2025, incorporating M9 = Reg (EU) 2024/1987) + http://publications.europa.eu/resource/oj/L_202401987.ENG.pdfa2a.L_202401987EN.pdf (OJ L 2024/1987, 31.7.2024)
rows.note: 0,10 mg/kg x 1000 = 100 ug/kg. Applies from 1 July 2025 per Article 10(1)(o) as inserted by Reg 2024/1987 Art 1(1)(b); Reg 2024/1987 Art 2: entry into force twentieth day after OJ publication of 31.7.2024, applies from 1 July 2025. The liquid sub-point carries no soy/non-soy split (the 0,40 soy value is powder-only, 3.6.13.2), so soy_class 'both' is consistent. Scope also covers follow-on formula, FSMP for infants/young children and young-child formula. EUR-Lex itself was unreachable (AWS WAF challenge on every URL form); the held consolidated PDF and the Publications Office OJ PDF were used instead. Latest amendment surfaced by search is Reg (EU) 2026/1825 (3-MCPD/glycidyl esters), which does not touch entry 3.6.

rows.scope: Annex I point 3.6.11 'Cereals', sub-point 3.6.11.3 'Husked rice' (carved out of 3.6.11.2 'Durum wheat (Triticum durum) and rice except products listed in 3.6.11.3')
rows.basis: No wet-weight or dry-matter remark is attached to 3.6.11/3.6.11.3; the only remark on 3.6.11 excludes cereals used for beer/distillates. Value stated as 2,0 mg/kg with the annex marker 'As from 1 July 2026'.
rows.evidence: "3.6.11.3 Husked rice 2,0 As from 1 July 2026" (Annex I pt 3.6.11.3; consolidated 02023R0915 08.10.2025 p. 58; OJ L 2024/1987 p. 6/7)
rows.note: 2,0 mg/kg x 1000 = 2000 ug/kg. Application date 1 July 2026 per Article 10(1)(p) (points 3.6.11.1 to 3.6.11.5) and the in-row 'As from 1 July 2026' marker; as of 2026-09-02 the level applies. Row basis 'product as placed on market' is not contradicted by the instrument, which states no separate basis for this row (unlike the wet-weight remarks on vegetables or the dry-matter remark on fresh seaweed). Food lawfully placed on the market before 1 July 2026 may remain on the market until its date of minimum durability or use-by date (Art 10(1) introductory phrase as replaced by Reg 2024/1987).

rows.scope: Annex I point 3.6.8 'Seaweed', sub-point 3.6.8.1 'Seaweed except products listed in 3.6.8.2' (3.6.8.2 = Wakame, 40 mg/kg)
rows.basis: For dry seaweed the maximum level applies to the product as placed on the market. For fresh seaweed the maximum level applies after washing and separating the edible part, on a dry matter basis (footnote 1: dry matter per Reg (EC) No 333/2007). Value stated as 30 mg/kg.
rows.evidence: "3.6.8.1 Seaweed except products listed in 3.6.8.2 30" (Annex I pt 3.6.8.1; consolidated 02023R0915 08.10.2025 p. 57; OJ L 2024/1987 p. 5/7)
rows.note: 30 mg/kg x 1000 = 30000 ug/kg. Applies from 1 July 2025 per Article 10(1)(o). Row scope 'seaweed except wakame' mirrors the instrument's carve-out exactly. Row basis 'product as placed on market' matches the instrument for DRY seaweed; for FRESH seaweed the instrument applies the same number on a dry-matter basis after washing/separating the edible part, which the register basis does not capture (not a mismatch, but worth a basis_class note if fresh seaweed is ever pooled).

rows.scope: Tenth Schedule (Regulation 31(1)) 'Maximum amounts of arsenic and lead permitted in food', item (b) Other Food, (2) 'Canned fish and meat, meat extract and hydrolysed protein', Arsenic (As) column
rows.basis: Schedule text: 'No article of food ... shall contain more than the amounts of the substances specified, in parts per million'; no as-consumed qualifier on this row (only the infant-formula lead cell is 'as consumed'). Regulation 31(1) prohibits import, sale, advertisement, manufacture, consignment or delivery of food exceeding the Schedule.
rows.evidence: "(2) Canned fish and meat, meat extract and hydrolysed protein 1 2" (Tenth Schedule (b)(2), Arsenic column; held PDF p. 211; SSO current version as at 02 Sep 2026)
rows.primary_source_used: https://sso.agc.gov.sg/SL/SFA1973-RG1?ProvIds=Sc10- (Singapore Statutes Online, Food Regulations, 'Current version as at 02 Sep 2026', read via browser) + raw/regulatory/sg/singapore-food-regulations-heavy-metals-2026.pdf ('Informal Consolidation - version in force from 30/1/2026')
rows.note: 1 ppm x 1000 = 1000 ug/kg. The Schedule column is 'Arsenic (As)' i.e. total arsenic, consistent with metal_species tAs; Singapore's inorganic-arsenic limits sit separately in reg 31(2)-(2B) (seaweed 2 ppm, polished rice 0.2 ppm, husked rice 0.35 ppm) and do not apply to this row. Row basis 'product as sold or imported' is a fair paraphrase of reg 31(1) read with the Schedule. Row amendment markers: [S 152/2017 wef 01/04/2017], [S 59/2019 wef 01/02/2019]. sso.agc.gov.sg returns 403 / a JS challenge to non-browser fetches; the browser load succeeded and matches the held PDF.

rows.scope: Tenth Schedule (Regulation 31(1)) 'Maximum amounts of arsenic and lead permitted in food', item (b) Other Food, (15) 'Fish, crustaceans and molluscs', Arsenic (As) column
rows.basis: Schedule text: amounts 'in parts per million' of the article of food; no as-consumed or dry-matter qualifier on this row. Regulation 31(1) prohibits import, sale, advertisement, manufacture, consignment or delivery of food exceeding the Schedule.
rows.evidence: "(15) Fish, crustaceans and molluscs 1 2" (Tenth Schedule (b)(15), Arsenic column; held PDF p. 212; SSO current version as at 02 Sep 2026)
rows.primary_source_used: https://sso.agc.gov.sg/SL/SFA1973-RG1?ProvIds=Sc10- (Singapore Statutes Online, Food Regulations, 'Current version as at 02 Sep 2026', read via browser) + raw/regulatory/sg/singapore-food-regulations-heavy-metals-2026.pdf ('Informal Consolidation - version in force from 30/1/2026')
rows.note: 1 ppm x 1000 = 1000 ug/kg. 'Arsenic (As)' column = total arsenic, consistent with tAs. Canned fish is governed by the separate row (b)(2) at the same 1 ppm. Mercury in fish is governed separately by reg 31(3) (predatory fish 1 ppm; other fish/fish products 0.5 ppm), not by this Schedule. Held PDF and live SSO text agree verbatim.

Attempted: raw/regulatory/fr/ (directory does not exist in the corpus); whole raw/ tree (no CSHPF/algues/DGCCRF file); DGCCRF 'ALGUES - Recommandations sanitaires pour l'emploi de preparations d'algues' (economie.gouv.fr CA_RS_Algues_Janvier2019.pdf: HTTP 403 via curl and WebFetch; browser load triggers a file-download dialog, not retried); CSHPF avis 01/1990 itself is listed by CEVA (Synthese 2024, refs) as 'non paru au Journal Officiel'. Secondary restatements read: https://www.anses.fr/fr/system/files/ERCA2017SA0070.pdf (ANSES 2020, Tableau 3), https://www.anses.fr/en/system/files/RCCP2007sa0007.pdf (AFSSA 2009), CEVA Synthese reglementaire 2024 (maj 7/01/2025).
rows.note: The register value 500 ug/kg dw equals the CSHPF recommendation as restated by ANSES (0,5 mg.kg-1 MS, from CSHPF sessions of 14 June 1988, 13 Dec 1988 and 9 Jan 1990) and by CEVA 2024 ('CSHPF 01/1990, AFSSA 04/2009'), and the status 'recommended maximum level' matches ANSES wording ('preconise', 'recommandee'). Not rated match because no primary CSHPF/DGCCRF text was read. In-force caveat: ANSES (21 July 2020) recommended lowering the Cd recommendation to 0,35 mg.kg-1 MS; the CEVA synthesis updated 7/01/2025 still lists 0,5 as the applicable French value and no DGCCRF adoption of 0,35 was located, so status is recorded as unknown rather than superseded. Action for the register owner: archive the DGCCRF Jan-2019 recommendations PDF (or the BID n 11/1987 CSHPF report) into raw/regulatory/fr/ so this row can be verified against a primary text.
